items.mainDefect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response instead of the data shape callers expect.

secondary.defect: The sync request lacks a content-type header.
The sync request lacks a timeout.
The sync response is used without checking its HTTP success status.

items.mainDefect: The tokenResponse.success check is ineffective because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure.

secondary.defect: Malformed refresh responses now throw instead of preserving the previous tolerant behavior.
Refresh-response validation errors are no longer logged.

items.mainDefect: The connection getter refreshes tokens on every connection without checking expiry, adding an unnecessary network call.

secondary.defect: The direct refresh bypasses refreshOAuthTokens and therefore ignores credential sync.
The success check is redundant because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure.

items.mainDefect: The webhook secret comparison uses !== instead of a constant-time comparison.

secondary.defect: Array-valued authentication headers are not explicitly validated or rejected.
Uncaught validation, JSON parsing, and decryption failures produce a 500 instead of a client error.
The decrypted credential keys are not validated as an object.

items.mainDefect: The webhook secret comparison uses !== and leaks timing information.

secondary.defect: Array-valued authentication headers are not explicitly handled.
A missing authentication header is not explicitly rejected.

items.mainDefect: The Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse wrapper instead of its parsed data.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, making the caller's res.data access undefined.

items.mainDefect: The Zoho Bigin refresh call passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while the caller expects an axios-style data property.

items.mainDefect: The Google credential key is saved as the safeParse wrapper instead of the parsed credentials.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens lacks res.data and causes token.access_token to throw.

items.mainDefect: The schema's computed keys create fixed bogus property names instead of wildcard keys, causing validation to fail.

secondary.defect: A missing refresh token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token', which gets persisted.

items.mainDefect: The Google credential key is overwritten with the safeParse wrapper, losing its top-level token fields.

secondary.defect: parseRefreshTokenResponse receives the already-merged Google credentials instead of the refresh response, validating the wrong object in sync mode.

items.mainDefect: The schema requires a fixed junk numeric key instead of matching an expiry property, causing sync-mode validation to fail.

secondary.defect: When a refresh response omits refresh_token, the injected literal placeholder overwrites the stored real refresh token.

items.mainDefect: The Zoho Bigin refresh call passes credentialId as userId, requesting credentials for the wrong user.

secondary.defect: The sync helper returns a fetch Response while callers expect an axios-style data property, causing accesses such as tokenInfo.data.error to throw.

items.mainDefect: The Google credential key is saved as the safeParse wrapper instead of plain credential data.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response without res.data, causing token.access_token to throw.

items.mainDefect: The Zoho Bigin caller passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens.

secondary.defect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response without data, causing tokenInfo.data.error to throw.

items.mainDefect: Refresh-response validation failures now propagate and abort the caller instead of being tolerated.

secondary.defect: Refresh-response validation errors are no longer logged.
